title: you can ask suspects ANYTHING in this LLM detective game
author: MorphLand
selftext:
Making a simple detective mystery game called Lurks Beneath where you interrogate suspects by asking  your own questions. No options or dialogue trees! Chuck here is sitting at that fire until his kid comes home, and he will answer whatever you actually type!

  
Lurks Beneath launches January 12, 2027.

  
This is my second game where I'm trying to incorporate NPCs w/ LLMs to make the worlds really come to life. Let me know what you think here! In this game there's a small trailer park, you walk around and can engage with three different people, cross examine, find environmental clues, etc. 

Anybody else working with NPCs and LLMs? Have posted here in the past and have had great discussions.

comments.author: curious_biped_dev
comments.body:
This is exactly the space I'm in too. I'm the solo dev behind s[TOR-Y]telling: Closed Loop, where the player is the narrator and a cast of characters improvise off whatever you actually write, no dialogue trees. Everything runs locally on a Llama-class model, so no accounts or per-message costs, which sounds like your setup too.

Curious how you're handling suspects staying consistent with clues they gave earlier once players start cross-examining and going off-script. That's the part I find hardest to keep coherent over a long conversation.

replies.author: MorphLand
replies.body: it's a lot honestly, lots of combining LLM plus keyword catching and lots of guardrails. The most important thing to me was bejing able to reduce response times so it actually feels like a game and not a gimmick. Small things help both that and the lore side like, put all WORLD lore first in the LLM so it doesnt have to keep warming up when you switch players.

comments.author: joeban1
comments.body: So who pays the fees for the LLM? The player or you?

replies.author: MorphLand
replies.body: It's locally bundled as part of the game, no tokens
